title: add-jsonschema-strict-response-format-openai-compat
author: Aisha Khan
description: Adds a first-class JSONSchema-backed response_format implementation with an optional strict mode and improved OpenAI-compatibility layer. This PR implements: 1) response_format parameter support across chat and completions endpoints; 2) server-side JSONSchema validation pass that returns structured errors with human-friendly messages and machine-readable codes; 3) strict mode which enforces exact schema conformance (no extra properties) and integrates with streaming to surface validation errors as early as possible; 4) compatibility translation layer for OpenAI-style 'response_format' and 'response_format_strict' flags and improved error mappings so downstream SDKs see consistent errors; 5) comprehensive unit and integration tests plus e2e examples and docs updates. Motivation: customers rely on structured output for deterministic downstream parsing; existing heuristics produced too many silent schema violations and inconsistent errors across endpoints. This PR centralizes the validation, standardizes error shapes, and adds a strict enforcement path for teams that require exact conformance. Implementation notes: validation happens in the API layer after model output assembly and prior to final content normalization; streaming improvements allow early speculative validation on chunks and will attach a final validation_result metadata block when streaming completes; when strict mode is enabled the service will return HTTP 422 with a structured error and hint to fallback to non-strict mode or to use relaxation rules. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains permissive; OpenAI compatibility flags are supported but mapped to Redwood's response_format types. Includes migration guide in docs and a console toggle for beta strict enforcement.

release_notes: Added response_format JSONSchema support with optional strict mode (beta)
Improved OpenAI compatibility flags for structured output and unified error mapping
Streaming validation hook to surface schema errors earlier during streaming responses
New console toggle to enable strict response_format enforcement per-tenant
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Default behavior remains permissive; existing clients not using response_format are unaffected. OpenAI flags are translated but behavior preserved unless strict mode enabled.
performance_notes: Benchmarks added to ci/workflows show median p50 API latency increase of ~1.8% for permissive validation at typical payload sizes; strict mode has larger cost and is gated behind feature flag and recommended for lower QPS or reserved capacity tenants.
security_considerations: Validator uses a sandboxed JSONSchema runtime with size bounds to avoid expensive patterns. Added CI fuzz tests to detect adversarial schemas. No secrets are logged in error payloads.
how_to_test: Run unit tests: pytest tests/unit -k response_format; integration: pytest tests/integration/test_response_format_strict.py; e2e: use tests/e2e/test_streaming_structured_output.test with local runtime. Feature flag can be toggled in console/feature_flags/response_format_strict_toggle.yaml for manual testing.
user_facing_error_examples: 422: response_format.strict_validation_failed - payload contains unexpected properties: ['metadata'] - suggestion: remove unknown fields or disable strict mode
400: response_format.invalid_schema - provided schema is not a valid JSONSchema draft-07 document - suggestion: validate schema against JSONSchema spec
409: response_format.conflicting_schema - requested schema conflicts with model output configuration - suggestion: use compatible schema or update model prompt
